start.text: Zara invites you to a small poetry night at a bookshop in Lahore. She's nervous - it's the first time she's reading her own ghazal in public. 'Tell me honestly,' she says, 'should I even go up there?'

choices.text: Of course - your words deserve to be heard.
Only if you want to. No pressure either way.

mid_reading.text: She steps up and reads, voice shaking at first, then steady. The room goes quiet, then erupts in applause. She finds your eyes immediately afterward.

choices.text: Tell her it was the best thing you've heard all year
Just smile and squeeze her hand

ending_gentle.text: She decides to sit this one out and just listen instead, leaning into your shoulder. 'Maybe next time,' she says softly. 'Thanks for not pushing.'

ending_proud.text: Zara beams, still a little breathless. 'I was terrified,' she admits, 'but you made me feel like it was okay to try.' She doesn't let go of your hand on the walk home.
